verdict: OK to lend in Manesar auto components — pursue tier-2/tier-3 suppliers to Maruti and EV-agnostic machined-part makers with tight covenants; avoid single-OEM, labour-exposed and pure-ICE-engine-part borrowers.
title: Manesar Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Manesar component maker buys steel, aluminium and bought-out castings, stamps or machines them, and sells into an OEM line that pays 45-90 days after a quality gate.** Cash is consumed at the input purchase and released only on OEM acceptance, so the working-capital cycle — not the margin — decides survival. Gross current assets for this peer set have averaged 160-170 days in recent years [10], so when a proposal lands, check the receivable-and-inventory days against that band; if the customer claims 90 days, ask for the OEM schedule and the actual collection statement.

## Where value and cash sit
**Pricing power sits with design complexity, not with volume.** CRISIL notes that complex systems such as diesel fuel injection carry real pricing power, while engine-and-related parts face higher obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11]. So when a proposal lands, check what share of revenue is engine-specific; if it is high, ask for the EV transition plan and the powertrain-agnostic order book. Peer ASK Automotive is already winning EV components across braking and aluminium lightweighting [5] — that is the template to lend to.

## What has changed now
**National auto-component output is running hot: IIP NIC 29 is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D].** Haryana GST is +10.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind. But bank credit to the sector is +27.0% YoY against output of +19.2%, a gap of +7.8 pp [D] — money is chasing this trade faster than it is producing. Peer Motherson Sumi Wiring grew revenue 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore with profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore [4], and Lumax beat Q2 2026 estimates and lifted its outlook [7]. Margins, though, are the soft spot: ASK flags aluminium squeezing margins [5] and Elara expects Q4FY26 EBITDA growth of about 21% with commodity risk [6].

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-2/tier-3 machined and lightweighting suppliers with two or more OEM customers, and EV-component wins on the books [5].** Avoid single-OEM dependents and labour-exposed units — the Manesar belt has a documented history of Maruti stoppages and worker disputes [1][2], and those sources are old, so treat them as pattern, not current fact. Structure with a receivables-backed working-capital line, a Debt/EBITDA covenant inside 2.5-2.75 times [10], and a monthly take of stock statements, OEM schedules, GST returns and a commodity-hedging confirmation [8].

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the credit-to-output gap [D] and commodity pass-through.** If a borrower's receivable days stretch past the 160-170 day peer band [10], cut limits and ask for the OEM reconciliation. If aluminium or steel input costs rise without a matching price revision [5][6], ask for the contract clause. If engine-part concentration is above half of revenue [11], ask for the EV order pipeline before any enhancement.
